summary: Verified all three bug fixes in this iteration. (1) Cancel-URL rollback: navigating to /app/participants?cancelled=1 while authenticated does POST /api/billing/v2/cancel-pending-addon on mount, shows a toast, and cleans the URL via history.replaceState — confirmed. (2) Over-limit banner: flipped cathy@example.com (3 active participants) to plan=solo temporarily; /settings/billing rendered the terracotta banner with copy 'You're over the Solo plan limit … $73.50 per fortnight … more than Family ($49.50)', both CTAs (over-limit-switch-family, over-limit-manage-participants) present. Restored plan to family after test. (3) Participants counter: tile reads '3 / 1 included' on Solo (was '3 / 2 included' in bug); current-plan-price shows '$73.50 per fortnight' and current-plan-breakdown reads '$24.50 base + 2 additional participants at $24.50 per fortnight each · Includes GST'. (4) DONE button code-review verified: skip-payment-btn shown when lastAdded.addon?.id present, add-done-btn shown otherwise (Participants.jsx L751-777). Backend cancel endpoint contract verified via 4 pytest cases (200 shape, idempotent second call = 0 cancellations, unauth 401/403, participants regression).

integration_issues.issue: Cancel-pending-addon toast fires twice on mount (React StrictMode double-invokes the useEffect since it has no guard/ref). Not visible in production build but is visible in dev. Consider a useRef guard.

action_items: Optional: guard the /app/participants ?cancelled=1 useEffect with a useRef so React StrictMode dev double-mount doesn't fire two toasts (only affects dev builds; production single-mounts are fine).
critical_code_review_comments: Participants.jsx L180-199 cancel-URL rollback useEffect has no in-flight guard; StrictMode dev double-invoke fires two POSTs (both return cancelled_count=0 the second time, but two success/info toasts render). Recommend a useRef sentinel: const ran = useRef(false); if (ran.current) return; ran.current = true;

Settings.jsx L432 still reads acctSummary.participants_active as the source of truth for count, but the fix intentionally moves participantsIncluded to PLANS[currentPlan].included_participants. That asymmetry is fine but worth a code comment noting that active count is authoritative from backend while included count is derived from the plan constant.

batch3_billing.py cancel_pending_addon does two updates in sequence (participant_add_ons then participants) without a transaction. If the process dies between the two writes, an add-on row is CANCELLED but the participant remains ACTIVE. Low probability but consider Mongo multi-document transactions or a single $set on both collections via a background reconciler.
